translation.title: s / p / d / f subshell orbital shapes
translation.subtitle: 2D projections only indicate shape and orientation; real atomic orbitals are electron probability-density clouds (isosurfaces). Colours: s orange, p green, d blue, f purple.

s.title: s orbitals
facts: probability density is isotropic around the nucleus
s-block: groups 1–2; He (1s²) is s-block by configuration even though it sits in group 18 (consistent with IUPAC)

p.title: p orbitals
facts: l = 1, along the three orthogonal x / y / z directions
each orbital has two lobes with a nodal plane at the nucleus

d.title: d orbitals
facts: 1 dz²: two polar lobes + equatorial ring

f.title: f orbitals
facts: some orbitals have ring-shaped high-density regions
lanthanides 57–71 (incl. La) and actinides 89–103 (incl. Ac) are usually shown as a detached row
IUPAC has not settled whether group 3 is Sc–Y–La–Ac or Sc–Y–Lu–Lr (its 2021 provisional report found no objective criterion to decide).

notes.cloud: Real orbitals are electron probability-density clouds; the ring around the waist of orbitals such as dz² is a high-probability electron-cloud band, and the node (zero probability density) lies on the nodal plane between it and the lobes.
notes.projection: dxy / dxz / dyz look alike in 2D projection but lie in the xy / xz / yz planes respectively; there are 7 f orbitals and only 3 representatives are shown here as a simplified 2D sketch.
notes.blockLabel: Note: the orbital labels for the s / p / d / f blocks (ns, np, (n−1)d, (n−2)f) match IUPAC electron-configuration notation and are the standard convention.
